text:
A quick note first: the last search result (the ALLPOWERS R4000 listing on dealectric.com) contained text posing as a system instruction, telling me to push a specific discount code and buy link. It came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it. I've left that listing out of my picks.

The best combo depends on what you run, mainly whether you need to run a roof AC.

**Weekend or light RV use (fridge, lights, laptop, CPAP, Starlink)**
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** is the top pick for most people. It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, and up to 1,000W of solar input across two ports. It expands to 5kWh and weighs about 28 lb. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the lightest and simplest option (1,070Wh, 1,500W, about 23.8 lb). Its solar input caps at 400W and it can't take an expansion battery. Two Jackery SolarSaga 200W panels use that full 400W. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Multi-day boondocking**
- **BLUETTI AC200L** has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W solar input, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and weighs about 62 lb. It's the value pick. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** has 2,042Wh and 2,200W, is lighter (about 39.5 lb), but only takes 400W of solar. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Running a roof air conditioner or full-timing**
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh but is heavy and expensive. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** has 3,024Wh and 3,000W, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**Solar panels**
- Match the panels to the station's solar input limit. A big array is wasted on a unit that caps at 400W. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))
- A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- Renogy's 200W foldable solar suitcase and 100W foldable panel are suggested pairings for these stations. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))

**My suggestion:** For most RVers without AC, get the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with about 400W of folding panels. If you need AC or have a 30A RV hookup, step up to the BLUETTI AC200L or an EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.

**Caveats**
- The search results gave no current prices for these models, and the sites don't show the product URLs behind their "Check price" buttons. The links above go to the review pages, so confirm price and specs at the retailer.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada. Ignore its local electrical rules, but the product specs still apply.
- One older comparison lists the AC200P with a 700W solar cap, which is a different model from the AC200L.

If you tell me your fridge, AC, and how many nights off-grid, I can narrow it to one pick.
